subject: Post-demo: parity qualification and proposed next tests (tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lin <kate.lin@datasol.com>, devops@datasol.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: parity qualification and proposed next tests (tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming)

Kate and team —

Thanks for running through the demo today. Helpful to see how you're thinking about embedding inference into the DataSol ingestion pipeline. To recap our conversation and propose a tight set of qualification tests so you can validate parity vs your hyperscaler proofs of concept:

1) Goal: validate functional parity and perf characteristics for three areas you flagged — function/tool-calling reliability, structured JSON output enforcement, and streaming (incremental partials + end-to-end latency).

2) Proposed minimal test plan (we can run these in your sandbox or our dedicated eval cluster):
   - Test A (Tool-calling): sequence of 50 simulated user sessions (stateful), each invoking 1-3 tools (search, db-write, code-exec). Verify call idempotency and retry behavior across transient failures.
   - Test B (Structured outputs): 200 prompt templates from your sample set (attached datasol-sample-prompts.jsonl). Validate strict JSON schema enforcement with automatic schema rejection vs soft-fix heuristics.
   - Test C (Streaming): sustained streaming at 5 qps for 10 minutes while measuring 95th/99th percentile first-token latency and tail token latency under KV cache warm/cold conditions.

3) What we need from you to run the above:
   - A small sample dataset (attached file or S3 link) and the JSON schema(s) you want enforced.
   - A short list of the critical tools (names + expected success criteria) you expect to call from the model.
   - Target concurrency and expected QPS (for streaming perf).

4) Deliverables from Redwood:
   - A short report with pass/fail per test and diffs vs the hyperscaler run you shared (we'll use identical prompts).
   - Reproduction scripts and a config bundle so you can re-run locally.
   - A follow-up call to review results and recommend any model/quantization/batching settings if we see a gap.

I've attached a parity checklist and the prompt set you dropped in the repo. Proposed timeline: start tests as early as Monday (2026-11-22) and ship results within 48 business hours after the run completes. If that works for you, please confirm and share the sample data link + any constraints (e.g., no PII).

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-parity-checklist.xlsx (xlsx), datasol-sample-prompts.jsonl (jsonl)
From: Kate Lin <kate.lin@datasol.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@datasol.com, procurement@datasol.com
Date: 2026-11-20T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: parity qualification and proposed next tests (tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming)

Thanks Evelyn — this looks good and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications:

- For Test A (Tool-calling), the highest risk is our db-write tool. We need to see at-least-once semantics with a clear retry window; if Redwood's recommended approach is at-most-once, we need to understand compensating controls.
- For Test B, we will provide two schemas: canonical-order-book.json and customer-profile.json. Enforce strict schema by default; if Redwood returns near-misses, we want a count and example.
- For Test C, please ensure you exercise both short (10-20 tokens) and long (300-800 tokens) streaming responses — we care about tail token latency.

We can make the S3 location available by EOD today: s3://datasol-eval/ds-parity-2026/ — credentials to follow via the secure share.

Also looping in procurement — we may need a short MSA addendum for the eval infra.

—Kate
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Kate Lin <kate.lin@datasol.com>, devops@datasol.com
Date: 2026-11-20T12:18:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: sequencing + quick differentiation notes (do not forward)

Rishi / Marissa —

Quick internal notes and suggested sequencing before we kick off the tests:

1) Prioritize Tool-calling topology: DataSol's failure mode is db-write duplication. Suggest we focus on idempotency tokens and transparent retry semantics — test both our function-calling contract and a fallback path where we emit an operation envelope for the client to execute. Measure the duplication rate under transient 100ms and 500ms error injectors.

2) For Structured outputs: enable strict schema enforcement in one pass and permissive-with-corrections in another — capture exact Levenshtein diffs for mismatches. This will let DataSol decide tolerance.

3) Streaming: use our dedicated eval cluster to simulate KV cache cold-starts and warm runs. Collect first-token and tail-token latencies, and also measure cost-per-token vs their hyperscaler logs (if they provide).

4) Model/infra knobs to try: small quantized variant for streaming, larger FP16 for tool-calling reliability. Note: batching can impact tail latency — we'll document per-test batching settings.

Action items: Rishi, can you provision the eval cluster slot for Mon AM and add the error-injection harness? Marissa, I'll send a short script to run the schema enforcement checks and produce the diff report.

Evelyn
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: sequencing + quick differentiation notes (do not forward)

+1 on the plan. Provisioning a dedicated 4-GPU eval cluster (A100 equivalent) for Mon 08:00–12:00 PST. I will wire up the transient error injector and the duplication meter.

Quick note on metrics collection: I'll output a single CSV (streaming-latency-template.csv) with fields: test_id, run_ts, qps, first_token_p95, first_token_p99, tail_token_p95, tail_token_p99, dup_rate, schema_fail_count, avg_cost_per_token. We'll attach this and a markdown summary.

Rishi
From: Kate Lin <kate.lin@datasol.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, devops@datasol.com, procurement@datasol.com

All — confirmed. We've shared the S3 link and sent credentials by secure share to evelyn@redwood.com. Procurement is happy to sign a short eval addendum; procurement@datasol.com will send a draft by tomorrow.

One ask: please include a short appendix explaining fallback behavior if the model cannot complete a tool call (we need to understand operational implications).

Looking forward to the results — Kate
